record.title: Google publishes ARTEMIS, an open-source agent for Android automation and testing
record.summary: Google’s public ARTEMIS repository provides natural-language Android automation through a reactive Flash profile and a slower plan-and-verify Pro profile, with CLI, Python SDK and MCP integrations for coding environments. The project describes accessibility-tree and OCR targeting with visual fallbacks, execution traces and history summaries. Its README claims 99%+ task completion on AndroidWorld’s 100+ multi-step tasks, but gives no model/version, per-task scores, trial counts or independent evaluation; this remains a first-party claim.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Google maintains a public Apache-2.0 repository with Android automation code, CLI, Python SDK and MCP integration; repository metadata reports creation on August 13, 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The project documents a Flash reactive profile typically taking 3–5 seconds per step and a Pro planning/verification profile typically taking 15–40 seconds per step, with different safety and reporting features.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The repository README claims 99%+ completion on AndroidWorld’s 100+ multi-step tasks; no benchmark protocol, model/version, trial count or independent evaluation is included in the inspected documentation.

evidence_gaps.description: The 99%+ AndroidWorld result is unsupported by a reproducible task-level result set or independent evaluation in the inspected repository.
The README omits a timing protocol and does not say whether its 3–5s and 15–40s figures include device, model/API and orchestration latency.

brief.importance_rationale: If the published implementation and stated behavior work as described, an open Android agent with CLI, SDK and MCP access can lower the cost of mobile-agent research and testing. The public documentation does not independently establish its 99%+ benchmark result or deployment reliability, so the consequence is meaningful but bounded.
limitations: The 99%+ AndroidWorld result is self-reported in the repository; the inspected README does not specify model/version, trial count, per-task scores or benchmark harness details.
No independent evaluation or installation/runtime test was performed.
Flash omits planning, pre-execution safety checks, checkpoint verification and final reporting; Pro is documented as materially slower per step.
The GitHub creation timestamp establishes repository creation metadata, not the exact time at which the project was publicly announced.
brief.summary: Google’s public ARTEMIS repository provides natural-language Android automation through a reactive Flash profile and a slower plan-and-verify Pro profile, with CLI, Python SDK and MCP integrations for coding environments. The project describes accessibility-tree and OCR targeting with visual fallbacks, execution traces and history summaries. Its README claims 99%+ task completion on AndroidWorld’s 100+ multi-step tasks, but gives no model/version, per-task scores, trial counts or independent evaluation; this remains a first-party claim.

technical.claimed_result: The README claims 99%+ task completion on AndroidWorld across 100+ multi-step tasks. It gives nominal typical per-step timings of 3–5 seconds for Flash and 15–40 seconds for Pro, without specifying the benchmark models/hardware or a timing protocol in the inspected text.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public repository, documentation and Apache-2.0 license are accessible. The documentation describes the profiles and interfaces; this activation did not install the software, run an AndroidWorld evaluation, or independently verify benchmark performance.
technical.mechanism: ARTEMIS exposes two profiles: Flash uses a reactive observe/act loop with history compression; Pro combines planning, tool-using operation, pre-action UI checks and a read-only checker. It targets Android via accessibility hierarchy, OCR and visual fallbacks, and exposes operation through a CLI, Python SDK and MCP server.
technical.regime: Public GitHub repository for natural-language Android automation on real devices or emulators; README documents 20+ apps and 100+ benchmark tasks, MCP/CLI/Python integrations and separate Flash/Pro profiles. Benchmark and timing details are project-authored; no independent run was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: The project cites Google Research’s AndroidWorld benchmark but does not provide matched competitor runs, full task-level results, model/version details or an external audit in the inspected repository documentation.

brief.title: Google publishes ARTEMIS, an open-source agent for Android automation and testing
brief.why_it_matters: A public, permissively licensed Android-control stack could make mobile-agent experimentation and automated UI testing easier to reproduce and integrate. The repository documents useful differences between low-latency reactive control and slower plan/verification, but the claimed benchmark success rate is not independently substantiated by the available materials.
